Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Mn to Scale AI Agents for Restaurant Businesses
Om Singh
| November 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million in funding from Houston-based Narahari Investments as it looks to expand its artificial intelligence solutions for restaurant businesses.
The fresh capital will support the expansion of its AI Catering Sales Agent, the launch of three additional AI agents currently in beta testing, and the development of a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.
Founded in December 2025 by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy , Kutlerri.ai is developing AI-powered tools to help restaurants generate more sales, control operating expenses and improve profitability. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.
Unlike conventional software providers that charge fixed subscription fees, Kutlerri.ai follows a performance-linked pricing model. Restaurants are charged based on the additional revenue generated or costs saved through its products.
AI Agent Helps Restaurants Find Catering Customers
Kutlerri.ai’s first commercially available product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, focuses on helping restaurants grow their catering businesses.
The agent identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius of a restaurant and reaches out to them through emails, text messages and phone calls. It also helps restaurants convert incoming enquiries into catering orders.
The product was developed in collaboration with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group operating in the Washington DC region.
According to Kutlerri.ai, its AI agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over a 10-month period. The startup said the revenue was more than 10 times the amount RASA paid for the service, without requiring the restaurant group to hire additional sales personnel.
Plans to Expand Product Portfolio and Team
Kutlerri.ai currently has one commercially available product, three AI agents undergoing beta testing and two more in development.
The latest funding will help the company accelerate product development, expand its teams and bring additional AI-powered solutions to restaurant operators.
The startup has more than 10 signed customers in the US, which remains its primary market. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also maintains an office in Houston.
Alongside its US expansion, Kutlerri.ai is exploring business opportunities in India and other markets.

Blitzy Focuses On Autonomous Software Development
Blitzy develops an AI-powered software engineering platform intended to help enterprises modernize legacy systems and accelerate new application development.
The company’s technology uses a proprietary ontology and graph-based architecture to develop a detailed understanding of large software codebases.
This approach is designed to provide AI systems with contextual information about how applications, components, and dependencies interact.
Using that information, Blitzy coordinates thousands of AI agents operating in parallel to perform software development tasks.
The platform is intended to address challenges associated with maintaining and updating complex enterprise software environments.
Large organizations frequently operate systems that have accumulated years of modifications, integrations, and dependencies.
Modernizing these environments can require significant engineering resources because changes to one component may affect other applications or business processes.
Blitzy’s approach seeks to improve efficiency by enabling AI agents to analyze software architecture and coordinate development activities.
The company also supports the creation of new software products, allowing engineering teams to use autonomous agents for development workflows.
For insurance companies and other financial services organizations, software modernization can be particularly important because many essential business processes depend on established technology systems.
Erie Strategic Ventures’ investment provides exposure to technology intended to improve enterprise software development and infrastructure management.
HiddenLayer Develops Security For AI Applications And Agents
HiddenLayer focuses on protecting AI systems against cyber threats throughout the development and deployment lifecycle.
Its platform supports security capabilities involving AI discovery, supply chain protection, attack simulation, and runtime defense.
These technologies are designed to help organizations identify and manage vulnerabilities associated with AI applications and infrastructure.
HiddenLayer’s platform addresses generative AI, predictive AI, and autonomous AI agents.
As enterprises integrate AI into business operations, they face security challenges that differ from those associated with conventional software systems.
AI applications can introduce risks involving model manipulation, unauthorized access, sensitive information exposure, and malicious interactions.
HiddenLayer develops tools intended to help security teams identify these risks and establish protective controls.
Its technology is supported by patented capabilities and adversarial AI research.
The platform includes tools for discovering AI systems within an organization and evaluating security weaknesses.
Attack simulation capabilities allow security teams to assess how AI applications may respond to malicious activity.
Runtime protection is designed to help defend deployed AI systems against threats during operation.
HiddenLayer also supports organizations seeking to protect intellectual property and meet applicable regulatory requirements.
The investment aligns with Erie Insurance’s interest in evaluating technologies that can support secure enterprise AI adoption.
Expanding Erie Insurance’s AI Innovation Strategy
Erie Strategic Ventures was established to identify emerging technologies with potential relevance to the insurance industry.
The fund invests across the personal and commercial insurance value chain while also evaluating adjacent markets.
Its investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer reflect two different areas of enterprise AI adoption.
Blitzy addresses the development and modernization of the software infrastructure that supports business operations.
HiddenLayer focuses on protecting AI applications and systems against emerging security threats.
Together, the companies represent complementary aspects of enterprise AI infrastructure.
Erie Insurance Senior Vice President for Next Level Innovation Keith Kennedy said the company is continuing to explore ways to apply AI safely.
The investments provide Erie with opportunities to engage with companies developing technologies that could influence how enterprises build and secure AI systems.
The company may also work with portfolio businesses as a customer or strategic partner.
